---
title: "Lab 00 — Reproducible R and a first statistical model"
output: learnr::tutorial
runtime: shiny_prerendered
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(learnr)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
source("lab_submission.R")
nh <- read.csv("data/nhtemp.csv")
n  <- nrow(nh)
m1 <- lm(temp ~ 1, data = nh)
m2 <- lm(temp ~ year, data = nh)
slope_of <- function(y) coef(lm(y ~ nh$year))[2]
lab_meta <- list(id = "lab00", title = "Reproducible R and a first statistical model",
                 open = c("q9", "q10"))
lab_prompts <- c(
  q1 = "How many observations does nhtemp.csv contain, and which years do they cover?",
  q2 = "The sample mean and sample standard deviation of the temperatures are about…",
  q3 = "Under model 1 (constant mean plus noise), the standard error of the mean is about…",
  q4 = "The slope of model 2 (temp ~ year), expressed per decade, is about…",
  q5 = "The residual sums of squares of model 1 and model 2, and the R-squared of model 2, are about…",
  q6 = "You simulate 20 series from model 1 (no trend) with set.seed(2027). How many have a fitted slope at least as large as the observed one?",
  q7 = "If we had 240 years from the same process instead of 60, what would happen to the sample SD s and to the standard error s/sqrt(n)?",
  q8 = "Which practice makes an analysis reproducible on a classmate's computer?",
  q9 = "Compare the 20 series simulated from model 2 with the observed series. Do they look alike? What does that say about model 2?",
  q10 = "Name one data-quality issue that could affect this temperature record and say whether more years of data would fix it."
)
```

## What you will do

Read the New Haven temperatures with a relative path, fit two models (constant mean, linear trend), simulate from them with a fixed seed, and interpret the numbers. Run the code boxes to get the numbers you need. At the end, download a `.txt` and upload it to Blackboard.

The data are already loaded as `nh` (columns `year`, `temp`). The two models are `m1 <- lm(temp ~ 1, data = nh)` and `m2 <- lm(temp ~ year, data = nh)`.

## Data and model 1

```{r peek, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=6}
str(nh)
range(nh$year)
mean(nh$temp)
sd(nh$temp)
sd(nh$temp) / sqrt(nrow(nh))
```

```{r q1}
  answer("365 daily values for 1971"),
```

```{r q3}
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

## Model 2: a linear trend

```{r trend, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=6}
m2 <- lm(temp ~ year, data = nh)
10 * coef(m2)["year"]
c(RSS1 = sum(resid(m1)^2), RSS2 = sum(resid(m2)^2))
summary(m2)$r.squared
```

```{r q4}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q4"]],
  answer("0.37 °F per decade: on average, the fitted mean temperature rises by about 0.37 °F every ten years", correct = TRUE),
  answer("0.037 °F per decade"),
  answer("-20.5 °F per decade"),
  answer("3.7 °F per decade"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q5}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q5"]],
  answer("RSS1 = 94.5, RSS2 = 70.0, R-squared = 0.26", correct = TRUE),
  answer("RSS1 = 70.0, RSS2 = 94.5, R-squared = 0.26"),
  answer("RSS1 = 94.5, RSS2 = 70.0, R-squared = 0.74"),
  answer("RSS1 = 1.27, RSS2 = 1.10, R-squared = 0.13"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

## Simulating from the fitted models

`simulate(m, nsim = 20)` draws 20 new data sets from the fitted model `m`. Always call `set.seed()` first.

```{r sim, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=10}
b1_obs <- coef(m2)[2]
set.seed(2027)
sims1 <- simulate(m1, nsim = 20)
slopes1 <- apply(sims1, 2, slope_of)
sum(slopes1 >= b1_obs)
round(10 * range(slopes1), 3)
set.seed(2027)
sims2 <- simulate(m2, nsim = 20)
matplot(nh$year, sims2, type = "l", col = "grey70", lty = 1, xlab = "Year", ylab = "deg F")
lines(nh$year, nh$temp, lwd = 2)
```

```{r q6}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q6"]],
  answer("None of the 20: without a trend, slopes stay between about -0.13 and 0.18 °F per decade, far below 0.37", correct = TRUE),
  answer("About 10 of the 20, as expected by chance"),
  answer("All 20, because the simulated series have the same mean as the data"),
  answer("It cannot be computed: simulated data have no slope"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```


## Submit

Type your name, download the text file, and upload it. Submit the questions first so the file contains your answers. If nothing downloads, the same `.txt` is in this folder: select it in the Files pane and choose Export.

```{r submit-ui, echo=FALSE}
shiny::textInput("student_name", "Your name", placeholder = "Name Surname")
shiny::downloadButton("download_txt", "Download submission .txt")
```

```{r submit-server, context="server"}
output$download_txt <- shiny::downloadHandler(
  filename = function() lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
  content = function(file) {
    write_lab_submission(
      path = file,
      name = input$student_name,
      lab_id = lab_meta$id,
      lab_title = lab_meta$title,
      state = learnr::get_tutorial_state(),
      prompts = lab_prompts,
      open = lab_meta$open
    )
    # The viewer in Posit Cloud often blocks the browser download.
    file.copy(
      file,
      lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
      overwrite = TRUE
    )
  }
)
```
